description: Full Oracle Select AI (DBMS_CLOUD_AI) coverage on an Oracle Autonomous Database: natural-language-to-SQL, chat, synthetic data, and RAG. SelectAIProvisionTool sets up the profile once on the target ADB; NL2SQLTool turns user questions into SQL/answers each turn (RUNSQL/SHOWSQL/EXPLAINSQL/NARRATE/CHAT/SUMMARIZE/TRANSLATE); CatalogMapTool discovers catalogs/schemas/tables; ConversationTool threads multi-turn chat; SyntheticDataTool populates tables with generated rows; VectorIndexTool builds RAG vector indexes. For plain SQL execution against an Oracle catalog, use AIDP's first-party SQL Tool (catalogType=EXTERNAL).

tools.description:
Provisions an Oracle ADB Select AI NL2SQL profile + agent tool so the companion NL2SQLTool can answer natural-language questions about a fixed set of tables. Runs DBMS_CLOUD_AI.CREATE_PROFILE + DBMS_CLOUD_AI_AGENT.CREATE_TOOL, records the result in an AIDP_NL2SQL_PROFILES audit table the tool auto-creates on first run, and is fully idempotent via a config-hash check.

When to use: Run this ONCE per (connection, schema, table set, model) combination, BEFORE the agent's first NL2SQL turn. Run again ONLY when the user changes the target tables/schema/model/credential — repeat calls with the same inputs are safe (skipped via hash). DO NOT use this for ad-hoc plain-SQL execution; for that, use AIDP's first-party SQL Tool (catalogType=EXTERNAL).

How to discover inputs: For `aidp_catalog_key`, call CatalogBrowserTool(list='catalogs') and ask the user which AIDP catalog binding exposes the target ADB. For `target_schema` + `target_tables`, ask the user — never default `target_tables` to a wildcard for schemas with many tables (Select AI prompts get huge fast; 8-20 tables is the sweet spot).

How to communicate: Report the action (`created` / `unchanged` / `recreated`) and the profile name in one sentence. On `unchanged`, tell the user the agent can proceed straight to NL2SQLTool with no further setup.

Example: SelectAIProvisionTool(aidp_catalog_key='construction_catalog.construction_schema.construction_db', profile_name='constr_demo', target_schema='ADMIN', target_tables='INCIDENT_REPORTS,WORK_ORDERS,EMPLOYEES') -> NL2SQLTool(profile_name='constr_demo', action='RUNSQL', prompt='how many open incidents last month?').

schema.name: profile_name
schema.description: Oracle identifier (<=120 chars) that names the Select AI profile + agent tool. Reused as the profile_name argument on every NL2SQLTool call. Example: `constr_demo`.

schema.name: target_schema
schema.description: Uppercase Oracle schema name that owns the listed tables. Required. Example: `ADMIN`.

schema.name: target_tables
schema.description: Comma-separated table names within target_schema. Order-insensitive (the tool sorts before hashing). Keep this list focused — Select AI accuracy degrades sharply past ~30 tables in a single profile. Example: `INCIDENT_REPORTS,WORK_ORDERS,EMPLOYEES`.

schema.name: comments
schema.description: Optional free-text description of the schema/tables fed to the LLM as a hint (helps accuracy). Example: `Construction site incident + work-order tables; PROJECT_ID joins to PROJECTS.PROJECT_ID`.
examples: Sales tables; ORDERS joins to CUSTOMERS on CUSTOMER_ID.

schema.name: force_recreate
schema.description: When true, drop and recreate the profile even if the config hash matches. Use only if you suspect the on-ADB state is corrupted.

credential_name.help: Display name of a SECRET_TOKEN credential in AIDPs Credential Store. Leave empty to fall back to resource_principal (which 401s against public AIDP data-plane endpoints per the Jun-17 thread).

aidp_credential_name.help: Display name of a SECRET_TOKEN credential in AIDPs Credential Store holding DB connect info (username, password, connection_string, wallet_b64). Distinct from the in-ADB credential_name above which is a DBMS_CLOUD credential.

_confDescriptions.aidp_catalog_key: Preferred: an AIDP catalog binding (catalog.schema.dbName) that exposes ADB credentials via get_connection_data. Find via AIDP Console → Catalogs. Leave blank if using the explicit conn_string/username/password/wallet fields.
_confDescriptions.conn_string: Fallback ADB connection string (TNS alias or full descriptor). Only use when aidp_catalog_key is blank. Example: `myadb_high`.
_confDescriptions.username: Fallback DB user. Only use when aidp_catalog_key is blank. Example: `ADMIN`.
_confDescriptions.password: (secret) Fallback DB password. Only use when aidp_catalog_key is blank.
_confDescriptions.wallet_b64: (secret) Base64-encoded wallet zip for the ADB. Only use when aidp_catalog_key is blank.
_confDescriptions.wallet_password: (secret) Wallet password (if the wallet is encrypted).
_confDescriptions.llm_model_id: OCI GenAI model id used by Select AI. Default `xai.grok-4`. Override only when the user explicitly asks. Catalog: .aidp/knowledge/oci-genai-models.md.
_confDescriptions.model_provider: Select AI provider. Currently only `oci` is supported by this toolkit.
_confDescriptions.credential_name: Oracle DB credential used by Select AI to call OCI GenAI. Default `OCI$RESOURCE_PRINCIPAL` (auto-created by `ENABLE_RESOURCE_PRINCIPAL`).
_confDescriptions.compartment_id: OCI compartment OCID for GenAI inference. OCI Console → Identity & Security → Compartments.
_confDescriptions.temperature: Select AI attribute: LLM sampling temperature (0-2). Leave blank for the provider default.
_confDescriptions.max_tokens: Select AI attribute: max output tokens for GENERATE. Blank = provider default.
_confDescriptions.seed: Select AI attribute: integer seed for reproducible generations. Blank = none.
_confDescriptions.conversation: Select AI attribute (true/false): enable conversation/chat history for this profile. Required before NL2SQLTool/ConversationTool can thread turns.
_confDescriptions.conversation_length: Select AI attribute: number of prior turns to retain when conversation=true.
_confDescriptions.constraints: Select AI attribute (true/false): send column NOT NULL / check / FK constraints to the LLM to improve accuracy.
_confDescriptions.annotations: Select AI attribute (true/false): include table/column annotations (data-dictionary metadata) in the prompt.
_confDescriptions.enforce_object_list: Select AI attribute (true/false): restrict the model to ONLY the tables in object_list (blocks queries against other tables).
_confDescriptions.object_list_mode: Select AI attribute: 'automated' or 'strict' — how the object_list is applied.
_confDescriptions.case_sensitive_values: Select AI attribute (true/false): treat literal values in the prompt as case-sensitive when generating SQL.
_confDescriptions.include_comments: Select AI `comments` attribute (true/false): send table/column comments to the LLM. Defaults on (helps NL2SQL). Distinct from the free-text `comments` provision param.
_confDescriptions.additional_instructions: Select AI attribute: extra free-text system instructions appended to every prompt for this profile.
_confDescriptions.embedding_model: Select AI attribute: embedding model id (used with vector_index_name for RAG).
_confDescriptions.provider_endpoint: Select AI attribute: override inference endpoint host for the provider.
_confDescriptions.auth_mode: OCI auth flavor for any ADB-adjacent OCI calls. `resource_principal` is the default (works inside AIDP compute).
_confDescriptions.fingerprint: OCI API key fingerprint. Auto-filled from ~/.oci/config.
_confDescriptions.private_key_content: (secret) PEM private key — only needed when auth_mode=user_principal.

tools.description:
Answers natural-language questions about Oracle ADB tables by calling DBMS_CLOUD_AI.GENERATE against a Select AI profile that SelectAIProvisionTool created. Returns rows (RUNSQL), just the generated SQL (SHOWSQL), a natural-language summary (NARRATE), or annotated SQL (EXPLAINSQL).

When to use: Use on every agent turn where the user asks a question about data in the ADB tables registered with the named profile. Default `action` is `RUNSQL`. For plain SQL execution where the user wrote the SQL themselves, use AIDP's first-party SQL Tool — this tool is for natural language.

How to discover inputs: `profile_name` comes from the SelectAIProvisionTool result. If the agent gets a 'profile not found' or ORA-20000-class error, call SelectAIProvisionTool FIRST then retry. For `prompt`, pass the user's question verbatim. For `action`, default to RUNSQL; pick NARRATE when the user wants a sentence answer instead of a table, SHOWSQL when the user is debugging the generated SQL, EXPLAINSQL when they want annotated SQL.

How to communicate: For RUNSQL, summarize row count + first 3 rows; for NARRATE, return the answer directly; for SHOWSQL/EXPLAINSQL, format the SQL in a code block. Read-only by construction: this tool refuses to execute generated SQL whose first keyword isn't SELECT or WITH, even if DBMS_CLOUD_AI returns DML — caller will see a `fail` envelope with a clear message, never a silent data mutation.

Example: NL2SQLTool(profile_name='constr_demo', action='RUNSQL', prompt='how many open incidents last month?', max_rows=100) → {ok: true, data: {sql: 'SELECT count(*) ...', rows: [{COUNT: 47}], rows_fetched: 1}}.

schema.name: profile_name
schema.description: Name of the Select AI profile created by SelectAIProvisionTool. Required. Example: `constr_demo`.

schema.name: prompt
schema.description: The user's natural-language question. Pass verbatim — DBMS_CLOUD_AI converts it to SQL using the profile's table list. Example: `how many open incidents last month?`.
schema.default: how many open incidents last month?
examples: how many open incidents last month?
top 5 employees by hours worked this quarter
sum of work-order costs grouped by project

schema.name: action
schema.description: Which DBMS_CLOUD_AI.GENERATE action to invoke. `RUNSQL` runs the generated SQL and returns rows (guarded read-only). `SHOWSQL` returns the SQL string only. `EXPLAINSQL` returns annotated SQL. `NARRATE` returns a natural-language answer with data. `CHAT` sends the prompt to the LLM as general chat (no schema grounding). `SUMMARIZE` summarizes the prompt/text. `TRANSLATE` translates it. Default `RUNSQL`.

schema.name: conversation_id
schema.description: Optional. A conversation id from ConversationTool(op=create). Pass it on each turn to thread chat history so the model sees prior context. Requires the profile to have conversation enabled (SelectAIProvisionTool conversation=true).

schema.name: max_rows
schema.description: Cap on rows fetched when action=RUNSQL. Default 100, hard ceiling 10000. Larger values can blow the agent's response budget.

aidp_credential_name.help: Display name of a SECRET_TOKEN credential in AIDPs Credential Store holding DB connect info (username, password, connection_string, wallet_b64). Distinct from the in-ADB credential_name above which is a DBMS_CLOUD credential.

_confDescriptions.aidp_catalog_key: Preferred ADB connection source. AIDP Console → Catalogs. Leave blank if using explicit conn_string/username/password/wallet.
_confDescriptions.conn_string: Fallback TNS alias or descriptor. Only use when aidp_catalog_key is blank.
_confDescriptions.username: Fallback DB user. Only use when aidp_catalog_key is blank.
_confDescriptions.default_action: Action used when the runtime param `action` is blank. Default RUNSQL.
_confDescriptions.max_rows: Default row cap for RUNSQL; runtime param overrides.
_confDescriptions.safety_check: When true, run SHOWSQL first and reject anything that isn't SELECT/WITH. Always recommended; turn off only for diagnostic builds.
_confDescriptions.auth_mode: OCI auth flavor for any OCI calls. `resource_principal` works inside AIDP compute.
_confDescriptions.fingerprint: OCI API key fingerprint. Auto-filled from ~/.oci/config.
_confDescriptions.private_key_content: (secret) PEM private key — only needed when auth_mode=user_principal.

tools.description: Discover the AIDP data landscape so the agent can find a catalog/schema/table to query and hand the user file locations. Walks catalogs -> schemas -> tables/volumes/knowledge bases and returns a nested tree + text summary; volumes include a /Volumes/<catalog>/<schema>/<volume> location. Pass catalog_key (a NAME) to scope, or omit to map everything. Uses the standard 5-key AIDP credential (conf.credential_name).

schema.name: catalog_key
schema.description: Optional. A catalog NAME (e.g. construction_catalog) to scope the walk to one catalog. Omit to map every catalog in the data lake.

credential_name.help: Standard 5-key AIDP credential (tenancy/user/fingerprint/private_key/data_lake_ocid). Region inferred; data_lake_ocid pulled from the bundle.

data_lake_ocid.help: Optional — comes from the credential bundle.

catalog_key.help: Optional — scope the walk to one catalog.

tools.description:
Manage a Select AI conversation (chat history) via DBMS_CLOUD_AI.CREATE_CONVERSATION / DROP_CONVERSATION so NL2SQLTool can thread multi-turn chat.

When to use: Call op=create ONCE at the start of a multi-turn NL2SQL session, then pass the returned conversation_id to NL2SQLTool on each following turn so the model remembers prior questions. Call op=delete to clean up. The profile must have conversation enabled (SelectAIProvisionTool conversation=true).

How to communicate: On create, report the conversation_id and tell the agent to reuse it. Uses the same ADB connection as NL2SQLTool.

Example: ConversationTool(op='create', title='Sales Q&A') -> {conversation_id: '4021'}; then NL2SQLTool(profile_name='sales_nl2sql', conversation_id='4021', prompt='and by region?').

schema.name: op
schema.description: `create` mints a new conversation and returns its id; `delete` drops the conversation named by conversation_id. Default `create`.

schema.name: title
schema.description: Optional short title stored on the conversation (op=create).

schema.name: description
schema.description: Optional longer description stored on the conversation (op=create).

schema.name: conversation_id
schema.description: Required for op=delete: the id returned by a prior op=create.

aidp_credential_name.help: Display name of a SECRET_TOKEN credential in AIDPs Credential Store holding DB connect info (username, password, connection_string, wallet_b64).

_confDescriptions.aidp_catalog_key: Preferred ADB connection source. AIDP Console → Catalogs. Leave blank if using explicit conn_string/username/password/wallet.
_confDescriptions.conn_string: Fallback TNS alias or descriptor. Only use when aidp_catalog_key is blank.
_confDescriptions.default_op: Op used when the runtime param `op` is blank. Default create.

tools.description:
Populate Oracle ADB table(s) with LLM-generated synthetic rows via DBMS_CLOUD_AI.GENERATE_SYNTHETIC_DATA. WRITE operation — it INSERTs rows, so it is gated behind confirm=true.

When to use: The user asks to fill a table with realistic fake/test data, or seed a demo schema. Single-table mode: pass object_name (+ owner_name, record_count, user_prompt). Multi-table mode: pass object_list, a JSON array of {"owner","name","record_count","user_prompt"}. Always confirm the target and row count with the user before setting confirm=true.

How to communicate: State exactly which table(s) and how many rows will be created, get the user's OK, then run with confirm=true and report success.

Example: SyntheticDataTool(profile_name='sales_nl2sql', object_name='CUSTOMERS', owner_name='SALES', record_count=200, user_prompt='realistic US customers', confirm=true).

schema.name: profile_name
schema.description: Select AI profile (from SelectAIProvisionTool) whose model generates the data. Required.

schema.name: object_name
schema.description: Single-table mode: the table to fill. Ignored when object_list is provided.

schema.name: owner_name
schema.description: Schema that owns object_name (single-table mode). Uppercase Oracle schema.

schema.name: record_count
schema.description: How many rows to generate (single-table mode).

schema.name: user_prompt
schema.description: Optional guidance for the generated data, e.g. value ranges or realism hints (single-table mode).
examples: realistic US customers with valid emails

schema.name: object_list
schema.description: Multi-table mode: JSON array of objects like [{"owner":"SALES","name":"CUSTOMERS","record_count":200,"user_prompt":"..."}]. When set, single-table params are ignored.

schema.name: params
schema.description: Optional JSON string of DBMS_CLOUD_AI tuning params (e.g. {"sample_rows":5,"table_statistics":true,"priority":"HIGH"}).

schema.name: confirm
schema.description: Must be true to actually INSERT rows. Safety gate against accidental data creation.

aidp_credential_name.help: Display name of a SECRET_TOKEN credential in AIDPs Credential Store holding DB connect info (username, password, connection_string, wallet_b64).

_confDescriptions.aidp_catalog_key: Preferred ADB connection source. AIDP Console → Catalogs. Leave blank if using explicit conn_string/username/password/wallet.
_confDescriptions.conn_string: Fallback TNS alias or descriptor. Only use when aidp_catalog_key is blank.
_confDescriptions.default_profile_name: Profile used when the runtime param profile_name is blank.
_confDescriptions.timeout: Connection + query timeout in seconds (synthetic generation can be slow).

tools.description:
Create or drop a Select AI vector index for retrieval-augmented generation via DBMS_CLOUD_AI.CREATE_VECTOR_INDEX / DROP_VECTOR_INDEX. Builds a vector store over documents in an object-store location and links it to a profile so GENERATE/NL2SQL can answer with retrieved context.

When to use: The user wants the agent to answer from documents (PDFs, text) in object storage rather than only SQL tables. op=create with location + object_store_credential_name + profile_name + vector_db_provider (usually 'oracle'). op=delete removes the index. Vector index builds can take minutes; wait_for_completion=true blocks until done.

How to communicate: Confirm the object-store location and profile with the user, then report the index name and completion state.

Example: VectorIndexTool(op='create', index_name='DOCS_IDX', vector_db_provider='oracle', location='https://objectstorage.../docs/', object_store_credential_name='OBJ_CRED', profile_name='docs_rag').

schema.name: op
schema.description: `create` builds the vector index; `delete` drops it. Default `create`.

schema.name: index_name
schema.description: Name of the vector index. Required for both create and delete.

schema.name: profile_name
schema.description: Select AI profile the index is attached to (create). Required attribute.

schema.name: location
schema.description: Object-store URI holding the source documents (create). Required attribute.

schema.name: object_store_credential_name
schema.description: DBMS_CLOUD credential that can read the object-store location (create).

schema.name: vector_db_provider
schema.description: Vector store provider for the index (create). Usually 'oracle'. Required attribute.

schema.name: attributes
schema.description: Optional JSON blob of any additional CREATE_VECTOR_INDEX attributes (vector_dimension, vector_distance_metric, chunk_size, chunk_overlap, similarity_threshold, match_limit, refresh_rate, pipeline_name, ...). Convenience params above are merged on top.

schema.name: description
schema.description: Optional description stored on the index (create).

schema.name: wait_for_completion
schema.description: When true (default), block until the index build finishes; when false, return immediately and let it build in the background.

aidp_credential_name.help: Display name of a SECRET_TOKEN credential in AIDPs Credential Store holding DB connect info (username, password, connection_string, wallet_b64).

_confDescriptions.aidp_catalog_key: Preferred ADB connection source. AIDP Console → Catalogs. Leave blank if using explicit conn_string/username/password/wallet.
_confDescriptions.conn_string: Fallback TNS alias or descriptor. Only use when aidp_catalog_key is blank.
_confDescriptions.default_op: Op used when the runtime param `op` is blank. Default create.
_confDescriptions.vector_db_provider: Default vector store provider merged into attributes when the runtime param is blank. Usually 'oracle'.
_confDescriptions.object_store_credential_name: Default DBMS_CLOUD credential for reading the object-store location.
_confDescriptions.vector_distance_metric: Optional default: distance metric (e.g. COSINE, EUCLIDEAN, DOT).
_confDescriptions.similarity_threshold: Optional default: minimum similarity for a match.
_confDescriptions.match_limit: Optional default: max chunks retrieved per query.
_confDescriptions.timeout: Connection + query timeout in seconds (index builds can be slow).
